findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category row matches
findings.body: The query at lines 9-11 returns a PG::Result. When no row matches, `[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the upgrade. This is the common case: embed_category only exists in site_settings if an admin set it (default ''), and the join requires it to equal an existing category name. The uncategorized fallback at lines 14-16 is only reached when the id is 0, which never happens for a real category, so the intended default is never applied. The empty result needs explicit handling, and the uncategorized_category_id lookup needs a guard too, since that setting may not be stored.

findings.title: Legacy host entries are copied without normalization, so existing embeds silently stop matching
findings.body: Entries from the old 'embeddable_hosts' setting are split on newlines and inserted verbatim. This bypasses EmbeddableHost's before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. The removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly accepted entries like 'https://eviltrout.com' (its spec covered that). Such sites get rows like 'https://eviltrout.com', but record_for_host compares against the URI host, so those rows can never match and embedding breaks for them after upgrade. Blank lines and trailing carriage returns from textarea input also become bogus rows. Each entry should be normalized, or invalid ones skipped, before insert.

findings.title: Host values interpolated into SQL without quoting
findings.body: The host string is interpolated directly into the INSERT statement. A value containing a single quote aborts the migration with a SQL syntax error. The pattern is also an injection vector if the setting value ever becomes less trusted. Use bound parameters or connection.quote.

findings.title: Migration is irreversible and create_table uses force: true
findings.body: `def change` contains raw `execute` calls, which Rails cannot invert, so rolling this migration back raises ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration. Separately, `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` (line 3) silently drops an existing embeddable_hosts table and its rows if one exists. Use explicit up/down methods and drop force: true.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. When host is nil (for example a create/update request without the host field, or a direct API call), this raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of a validation error. The callback should guard against nil.

findings.title: Stored hosts with a port can never match a lookup
findings.body: The format validator explicitly allows an optional port, e.g. 'eviltrout.com:8080'. But record_for_host (line 14) looks up by URI#host, which drops the port, so a host saved with a port never matches and embedding silently fails for it. Either reject ports in validation or compare including the port.

findings.title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the parameter
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the parameter. The parameter is `uri.host` taken directly from the referer or embed_url, so a request from 'http://EvilTrout.com/...' is rejected even though the host is allowed. The parameter should be downcased.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts allowed and lookup returns an arbitrary row
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or unique index on host, and the admin UI can add the same host twice. `.first` has no ORDER BY, so record_for_host returns an arbitrary row, and TopicEmbed.import will use an arbitrary category for that site. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index.

findings.title: TLD length limit rejects valid domains
findings.body: The TLD pattern `[a-z]{2,5}` rejects valid hosts with longer TLDs such as example.community or example.technology. The setting this replaces accepted any string, so admins with such sites can no longer configure them.

findings.title: update and destroy crash with a 500 on unknown id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` then raises on `nil.host=`, and destroy (line 16) raises on `nil.destroy`. A double-click on delete or a stale client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Use find or check for nil.

findings.title: category_id is never checked against existing categories
findings.body: The submitted category_id is only defaulted when blank. It is never checked against Category, and the column has no foreign key. A nonexistent id is stored, and TopicEmbed.import then passes it to PostCreator, creating topics in a missing category. The same happens after a category is deleted. Validate that the category exists.

findings.title: Admin hosts controller has no behavioral tests
findings.body: The only spec asserts that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController. Nothing exercises create, update, destroy, the uncategorized default in save_host, validation failures, the not-found path, or non-admin access. The core of the new write endpoint is untested.

findings.title: Fabricator contents are swapped between the two files
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now contains only the :embeddable_host fabricator, while the category, diff_category, happy_category and private_category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabrication still loads both files, but the names mislead anyone looking for the category fabricators and make the diff read as a deletion.

findings.title: _hydrateEmbedded now rewrites every *_ids key and can leave undefined entries
findings.body: The regex now matches every `*_ids` key in REST-serialized payloads, and the original key is deleted. When the referenced collection is not in the root payload, _lookupSubType returns undefined for each id, so the result is an array of undefined values. The `hydrated || []` fallback never runs because map always returns an array. Previously such keys were left intact, and now the id list is lost and consumers get undefined items. This matters for the new feature: EmbeddingSerializer uses `embed: :ids` without `include: true`, so the root may have no embeddable_hosts collection and the admin list would iterate undefined hosts. Unresolved ids should be filtered out, and conversion should only happen when the collection is present.

findings.title: find embedded test passes for the wrong record
findings.body: The test calls store.find('fruit', 2) but asserts apple's data. The /fruits/:id pretender in create-pretender.js.es6 (line 227) always returns fruits[0] regardless of the id, so the change from id 1 to 2 has no effect and the test would still pass if lookup by id were broken. The fixture should use request.params.id.

findings.title: Stale test named for a host check that no longer exists
findings.body: The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' sets up no host. expandable_first_post? no longer checks hosts, and embed_truncate defaults to false, so the test passes trivially and no longer tests what its name says. It should be removed or rewritten to test the behavior that actually matters.

findings.title: Delete has no error handling
findings.body: delete() calls destroyRecord().then(...) with no failure handler, unlike save() which uses popupAjaxError. On a server error the row silently stays with no feedback, and the promise rejection is unhandled. A .catch(popupAjaxError) is needed.
